title: Share the code, not just the data: A case study of the reproducibility of articles published in the Journal of Memory and Language under the open data policy

cost.compute_notes: PsyArXiv preprint PDF 517 KB (DOI 10.31234/osf.io/hf297), read as `pdftotext -layout` (1,657 lines), methods and results in full. Published version is Elsevier and paywalled; the preprint is the version read and its Data Availability statement is the one audited. Artifact audit via the OSF API (nodes, files, providers, children, wikis) and the GitHub API. No analysis re-run: the code that would have been re-run is the thing that is missing.

claims.statement: The Journal of Memory and Language's 2019 open data and code policy raised the rate of data sharing by more than 50 percentage points, from 20 of 59 papers before to 51 of 59 after; but 8 of the 59 post-policy papers still had inaccessible data, and only 75% of those that were accessible shared all the data needed to reproduce the reported analyses.
claims.scope: 59 papers immediately before and 59 immediately after the policy took effect. 'Accessible' means at least some subset of the described data was obtainable, deliberately generous.

quantities.name: code_sharing_rate_given_data_shared
quantities.unit: proportion of papers with accessible data
quantities.baseline: post-policy; the policy requires code as a rule

quantities.name: complete_data_rate_given_data_shared
quantities.unit: proportion of papers with accessible data
quantities.baseline: post-policy; all variables reported in the manuscript present in the file

our_assessment.why: Counts are printed with their denominators throughout and the reasons for the 8 inaccessible cases are itemised, including one where a repository demanded a stated purpose and the authors declined to say they were running a reproducibility check -- a scruple most such studies do not report.

claims.statement: Under a strict criterion (every reported analysis reproduces exactly, rounding aside), 1 of 19 papers that shared data but no code reproduced, against 19 of 32 that shared both. Under the most lenient criterion tolerating up to 20 discrepancies over 10%, the figures are 7 of 19 and 26 of 32. Overall reproducibility is 34% to 56% of the 59 surveyed papers depending on the criterion.
claims.scope: Post-policy papers only. Authors were deliberately NOT contacted for clarification -- unlike Hardwicke et al. -- on the ground that an analysis step documented only privately is not reproducible for a reader.

quantities.baseline: data shared, NO analysis code; strict criterion

quantities.baseline: data AND analysis code shared; strict criterion

our_assessment.why: This is the cleanest reproducibility funnel in the area file: every rung printed, both the numerator's own denominator and the widest one, and a criterion ladder at K = 1, 5, 10, 20 rather than a single line drawn where it flatters. The ratio between the strictest and most lenient reading of the SAME attempts is 34% to 56% -- a factor of 1.6 from the criterion alone, before any denominator argument. That is the same lesson as maria2026-executability-denominators from the other direction: there the denominator moved the number by 2x, here the criterion moves it by 1.6x, and neither is visible in a citation.

claims.statement: In a Bayesian logistic regression, the availability of analysis code raises the probability of reproducing a paper by about 38 percentage points; a readme file and preregistration have effects that are not distinguishable from zero.
claims.scope: 51 post-policy papers with accessible data. Predictors: code, readme, preregistration, each 0/1. Regularising priors N(0, 1.2) on the intercept and N(0, 1.5) on slopes.

quantities.name: reproduction_probability_given_data_only
quantities.baseline: intercept: data shared, no code, no readme, no preregistration; strict criterion

quantities.name: reproduction_probability_increase_from_sharing_code
quantities.baseline: strict criterion; log-odds 2.49, SE 0.76, 95% CrI [1.11, 4.08], odds ratio 12.1

quantities.name: reproduction_probability_increase_from_sharing_code
quantities.baseline: most lenient criterion; intercept rises to 39% but the code effect is unchanged

our_assessment.why: Observational: papers that share code are plausibly written by more careful people, and the same 'disposition' confound bit our own analysis of the Samuel & Mietchen corpus, where a Makefile and a CITATION.cff predicted installability while the environment files did not. What makes this one more than a care proxy is that the authors ALSO modelled readme and preregistration -- two other care markers -- and both come out indistinguishable from zero while code does not. That is not identification, but it is the right control to have run, and almost nobody in this literature runs it. THE EFFECT SIZE IS THE LARGEST WELL-ESTIMATED ONE IN THIS AREA: +38 points against a pinning effect that is null once dependency count is controlled, and a containerisation effect nobody has measured at all.

claims.statement: OUR ARTIFACT AUDIT. The analysis code for this paper is not retrievable from the address the paper gives. osf.io/3bzu8, named in the Data Availability statement as holding 'the code and anonymized data for regenerating this paper', is a public node with zero files in OSF storage; its GitHub add-on points at github.com/annlaurin/reproducibility, which returns 404, as does github.com/annlaurin/images, the repository hosting the figure embedded in that node's own wiki.
claims.scope: Checked 2026-08-25 against the preprint's Data Availability statement, which is the version read here; the published Elsevier version is paywalled and may name other locations. The author's GitHub account is active and holds six other public repositories, and a GitHub search restricted to that user for 'reproducibility' returns nothing, so this is not a rename that a reader could follow.

quantities.name: artifact_locator_resolution_rate
quantities.unit: proportion of the paper's two stated artifact URLs
quantities.baseline: osf.io/3x2y6 (the 59 reproduction attempts) resolves and is intact in per-paper components; osf.io/3bzu8 (the paper's own code and data) does not lead to any file

our_assessment.why: Established by the OSF API (node public, osfstorage empty, provider list shows a github add-on, add-on folder_id 'annlaurin/reproducibility') and the GitHub API (404 on that repository, 404 on annlaurin/images, 0 results for a user-scoped search, 6 unrelated public repositories on a live account). NOT A GOTCHA, and the tone matters: this is evidence FOR the mechanism the authors identified, not against them. Their DATA survived -- the 59 per-paper reproduction attempts are intact in components -- and their CODE did not, because code was shared by LINKING a mutable repository from an archive rather than by DEPOSITING it in one. The paper's own finding, instantiated on the paper. What it adds to their recommendation is a distinction they do not draw: sharing is not depositing. An OSF GitHub add-on is a pointer, and a pointer inherits the lifetime of what it points at.

claims.statement: Reproducing 232 reported values from raw data cost Artner et al. 280 workdays, and even then 70% was reached only by trying analyses that conflicted with the reported procedure.
claims.scope: Reported by these authors when comparing their own effort to Artner et al. 2021 (Psychological Methods), not measured here.

quantities.name: verification_cost_workdays_per_reported_value
quantities.baseline: Artner et al. 2021: 280 workdays for 232 reported values in 46 articles

our_assessment.why: Second-hand and not checked against Artner et al. directly. Recorded anyway because the COST side of verification is nearly absent from this area file and this is the only per-value figure in it. If it survives checking it is the number that decides whether any third-party verification scheme can scale: at 1.2 workdays per reported value, checking one ordinary paper's forty numbers is two person-months.

checked.how: curl -s https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/3bzu8/ ; .../files/osfstorage/ ; .../files/ ; .../children/ ; .../wikis/ ; .../addons/github/ ; then curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/annlaurin/reproducibility and .../annlaurin/images and /users/annlaurin/repos
checked.result: Node is public, titled as the paper, last modified 2022-04-18, has a wiki, and has ZERO files in osfstorage and ZERO children. Its provider list includes a `github` add-on whose folder_id is 'annlaurin/reproducibility:'. That repository returns 404, as does annlaurin/images which hosts the figure the wiki embeds. The account is live with 6 unrelated public repos. This is the address the paper gives for its own analysis code.

Public. osfstorage holds IDs.pdf (32,652 bytes), IDs_pre_policy.csv (5,456 bytes) and a Wiki images folder; the 59 per-paper reproduction attempts are in CHILD COMPONENTS (Paper13, Paper38, Paper39 ... at least 10 on the first page). A listing of osfstorage alone shows 3 items and looks nearly empty -- which is how this artifact would be mis-scored as insufficient by any check that does not follow the component indirection.

Re-runs the whole audit from the two OSF node ids and prints every intermediate: node metadata, storage providers, file counts, children, wiki text, the github add-on's folder_id, and the GitHub API's answer for each repository named. Written so the claim can be re-checked in one command rather than eight.

relations.why: Independently, and this is the kind of agreement that counts. Hardwicke found that a mandatory open-DATA policy moved availability to ~99% while analysis-script sharing went 8.7% to 6.0%, i.e. not at all, and that the dominant cause of irreproducibility was under-specification of the analysis. This study, on a different journal, a different field, a different team and a manual rather than automated method, finds the executable specification worth +38 points. Different implementations, so the agreement carries information -- see instance-general/philosophy-of-science/independence-the-hidden-premise-of-agreement.md.
relations.asymmetric_note: Not directly poolable: Hardwicke contacted authors and this study deliberately did not. Hardwicke's UNAIDED figure is the comparable one.

relations.why: Same failure in a different technology, and each is the other's generalisation. Malka: 57% of Docker images pushed to a registry were gone in under two years. Here: the repository backing a published paper's OSF code node is gone in four. In both cases what was archived survived and what was LINKED did not. The distinction that matters is not built-vs-declared, it is DEPOSITED vs POINTED-AT.

Adds a criterion ladder to a synthesis that only had a denominator ladder. The same 59 papers score 34% or 56% depending on how many >10% discrepancies are tolerated -- a factor of 1.6 from the criterion alone, before any denominator argument. Every rung is printed, which makes this the model of reporting the area file has been asking for.

On which recommendation is worth making. Trisovic's list leads with pinning versions and containerisation; on this evidence the intervention with by far the best-estimated effect is simply SHARING THE ANALYSIS CODE AT ALL (+38 points, CrI [19, 60]), against a pinning effect that is null once dependency count is controlled and a containerisation effect nobody has measured. The field has been optimising the environment while the specification was missing.

Reciprocal of the mirror image. 'Sharing is not depositing' names a deposit that resolves and contains nothing; this one names a deposit that is complete for REPRODUCTION and incomplete for ADJUDICATION -- it settles every number the authors print and cannot settle the leading alternative explanation of their finding. Both pass every artifact badge in existence.

open_questions: Is Artner et al.'s 280 workdays for 232 values right? It is the only per-value cost figure in this area and it decides whether third-party verification can scale at all. Recorded second-hand and unverified; the paper is Psychological Methods 10.1037/met0000365 and its data location was not found in two attempts. ATTEMPTED AND FAILED 2026-08-25: OpenAlex and Unpaywall both report is_oa=true with exactly one location, a KU Leuven bitstream path that returns 404 because the repository migrated to a new discovery interface. The publisher version is APA and paywalled. So the number stays second-hand -- and the failure is itself an instance of the pattern in instance-general/philosophy-of-science/the-specification-execution-gap.md: the SPECIFICATION of openness is indexed and intact while the EXECUTION fails.

How many other papers in this area have lost their own code? The check is cheap and mechanical -- resolve each artifact URL, and where it is an archive node, follow the provider indirection to whatever it actually points at. This corpus's own records would be a fair place to start, and `kb.py links` currently CANNOT do it: it checks the URL and would have scored osf.io/3bzu8 as alive.

Does the code effect survive matching on care? The authors control for readme and preregistration and both come out null, which is the right test and a weak one at n=51. A larger corpus with more care proxies -- the Makefile and CITATION.cff markers that predicted installability in samuel2024#c7 would do -- could separate 'code helps' from 'code marks a careful author'.

The criterion ladder (K = 1, 5, 10, 20) is the best feature of this design and nobody else uses it. Re-scoring an existing corpus at several K would show whether the field's disagreements are about denominators, criteria, or the world.
